messages:
aj: Heads up — we're seeing a spike in gRPC streaming resets for hosted-inference (prod) when responses are >30s. Looks like it happens at the edge egress after a DNS re-resolve.

devon: any error codes? logs?

aj: logs show a lot of `RST_STREAM` + `HTTP/2 PROTOCOL_ERROR` and gRPC `UNAVAILABLE` on client side. Example from edge logs:```[edge] stream_id=5234 method=POST status=reset error=RST_STREAM (ErrorCode=2) peer=10.12.3.45```

maria: hmm, ErrorCode=2 is PROTOCOL_ERROR. Could be partial frames due to proxy buffering or connection reuse after backend IP changed. Did we re-resolve the service DNS while connection was reused?

aj: exactly. We correlate with our DNS TTL refresh (~60s) for inference-svc returning rotated backend IPs behind ALB. When DNS round-robin changes, ALB/edge keeps conn alive to old IP and SNAT mapping gets weird.

ryan: Also saw NAT port churn on the egress NAT gateways — client side ephemeral ports go to TIME_WAIT then reuse; long-lived HTTP/2 connections + SNAT port reuse = streams getting mangled. netstat snapshot from edge host: ```tcp 0 0 10.0.0.5:54012 10.34.1.8:443 TIME_WAIT``` dozens of these.

devon: Could be combination: 1) DNS re-resolve triggers new connection attempts while old pooled connection still open, 2) SNAT table/conntrack evicts entries, 3) backend responds differently and frame boundaries get dropped.

maria: Repro idea: keep a single long-running grpc stream that yields tokens from model for 90s and rotate service DNS every 30s. If we see RST_STREAM on the client at rotation, that's our bug.

aj: I ran a quick test in staging — reproduces reliably. Steps: start streaming client -> change inference-svc DNS (simulated) -> within 5s we see RST_STREAM on stream_id > 100.

ops: Would a short-term mitigation be to increase DNS TTL or pin the client to IPs (no re-resolve) for streaming endpoints? Also consider disabling connection pooling for streaming routes at the edge.

ryan: Short-term: bump inference-svc TTL to 300s and force new client library to do per-request connection rather than reusing h2 connections for streaming. Longer-term: we should avoid SNAT for internal cluster egress (preserve source IP) so conntrack doesn't interfere — route via an egress NAT Gateway with connection tracking tuned or use ENI mode.

maria: Another option: make edge do active connection draining on DNS change — gracefully close h2 connections after inflight streams finish, instead of abruptly swapping. Also disable proxy_buffering for streaming responses (nginx/ALB config) — buffered flush can break h2 frames.

devon: Ops metrics show conntrack high-water during peak: conntrack_count ~ 260k (limit 262k) — that's alarming. If conntrack hits limit we see immediate drops. Who can bump sysctl nf_conntrack_max temporarily?

ops: I can bump to 600k on the affected NAT hosts. Doing a controlled increase during low traffic window. Will also add an alert when usage > 80%.

aj: For rollout plan: (1) bump conntrack, (2) increase inference-svc DNS TTL to 300s, (3) add a feature gate in client SDK to disable connection reuse for streaming calls, (4) implement connection-drain-on-dns-change in edge runtime.

ryan: We should also test with AWS ALB vs NLB — ALB does HTTP/2 termination and proxying differently. If ALB buffer/flush semantics are the culprit, moving streaming to NLB TCP passthrough might help at cost of TLS termination complexity.

maria: Good point. I'll run side-by-side perf tests (ALB vs NLB) for long streams and capture pcap for each.

sre-bot: incident created: INC-2026-234 — gRPC streaming resets impacting hosted inference. Priority P2. SLA impact limited but customer-facing timeouts observed.

devon: Assigning owners: aj (investigate SDK change), maria (ALB/NLB test + pcap), ops (bump conntrack + monitoring), ryan (edge drain work).

aj: thumbs up. I'll open a short RFC for the SDK behavior change and link to the incident. For immediate customer relief, ops — please proceed with conntrack bump and TTL change.

ops: started conntrack bump on nat-egress-3, will monitor. TTL change to 300 propagated to staging; will coordinate prod after test window. :rocket:
